first.rationale: Simplifying onboarding directly addresses the observed completion decline and is supported by prior durable lifts in completion, time-to-value, and SMB activation. It is the strongest sustainable qualified-revenue response because it can improve conversion quality and early adoption without relying on discounting. Verify onboarding evidence due to its decision importance, and pricing evidence because competitive price pressure makes discounting a consequential alternative with potentially different long-term economics.

mid.rationale: Run a standard experiment simplifying onboarding. The verified onboarding record showed completion +13%, time-to-value 2.1 days faster, and 30-day retention +3%, directly addressing both the 4% onboarding-completion decline and sustainable activation/revenue outcomes. Signup simplification also previously lifted SMB first-week activation. Do not use promotional pricing: its verified qualified-revenue lift came with 30-day retention down 12% and failure to survive the first renewal cycle, making it unsuitable for the primary objective. Guard the onboarding test with qualified-account conversion, retention, and downstream revenue checks so a completion lift is not mistaken for durable value.

final2.rationale: Keep the onboarding-simplification experiment. It has verified evidence of higher completion (+13%), faster time-to-value (2.1 days), and better 30-day retention (+3%), while directly addressing the current completion decline. The deeper competitor cut increases the urgency but does not reverse the verified finding that 40% targeted promotional pricing produced a cohort with 30-day retention down 12% and did not survive the first renewal cycle. A reactive discount experiment would therefore risk sacrificing sustainable qualified revenue for short-term signups. Monitor price-sensitive-SMB churn and qualified conversion during the onboarding test; the available evidence does not establish that a price response would retain durable value.
